# sigma_plugin (Resource)

A Sigma custom plugin (beta API). Sigma loads the plugin from `url` when it is added to a workbook, and from `dev_url` when the plugin runs in development mode.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Sigma custom plugin (beta API).
#
# Sigma loads the plugin from `url` when it is added to a workbook, and from
# `dev_url` when the plugin runs in development mode. Both default server-side
# when omitted (url to empty, dev_url to http://localhost:5173).
resource "sigma_plugin" "my_chart" {
  name        = "My Custom Chart"
  description = "A bespoke visualization element."
  url         = "https://plugins.example.com/my-chart"
  dev_url     = "http://localhost:5173"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the custom plugin.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the custom plugin.
- `dev_url` (String) Development URL for the plugin. Sigma loads the plugin from this URL when it runs in development mode. Defaults to `http://localhost:5173` when omitted.
- `url` (String) Production URL where the plugin is hosted. Sigma loads the plugin from this URL when it is added to a workbook. Defaults to an empty string (no production URL set) when omitted at creation; removing it later keeps the current value, so set `""` to clear it. Sigma's API can't change it in place, so changing it replaces the plugin, which gets a new `id`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier (UUID) of the custom plugin (`pluginId`).
- `type` (String) Plugin type. Currently always `element`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sigma_plugin.example '<plugin_id>'
```
